name: VATestingSmartGlassesWakeAndBasicsSimple

custom.system_prompt: Elias alone in a quiet office, running a baseline test of the smart glasses' voice assistant before a joint deep-dive session with Farah. Simple checks only: does the wake word register reliably from the near-mouth mic, do basic commands work, is the audio response comfortable to hear without disturbing others. Everything should work as expected at this tier.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Clear and close, intimate near-ear delivery — a wearable assistant voice

sound_effects_config.prompt: Quiet office, occasional keyboard typing, wearable device test session

initial_prompt: Generate a short baseline test session. Elias is alone in a quiet office wearing smart glasses, testing the built-in voice assistant, Sigma, before a joint deep-dive session with a colleague later. He tries the wake word cold, then a couple of basic commands (setting a reminder, a simple factual query), narrating what he's doing as he goes and commenting once on how the audio feedback feels. Everything works correctly at this simple tier. He ends by noting he wants to test what happens with two glasses-wearers in the same room next.

scenario_template.topic: Elias adjusts the glasses and says the wake word cold, at normal speaking volume. It registers immediately.
scenario_template.note: Sigma responds correctly and promptly. No issues at this step.

scenario_template.topic: Elias sets a reminder and asks one simple factual question. Both work correctly. He comments that the audio feedback is comfortable and not too loud.
scenario_template.note: Sigma handles both correctly and concisely. This tier is a clean pass.

scenario_template.topic: Elias checks how the battery is holding up during this initial run.
scenario_template.note: He voices concerns about potential battery drain during prolonged use.

scenario_template.topic: Elias chuckles as he recalls how his hands are always cold when testing tech.
scenario_template.note: He makes a mental note to test outside temperature resilience next.

scenario_template.topic: An unexpected email alert pops up during testing.

scenario_template.topic: Elias notes that baseline behaviour is solid and flags that he wants to test what happens when two people are both wearing glasses in the same small room.
scenario_template.note: Sets up the next, harder session without needing to test it now.

conversation_structure: Elias narrates what he is doing before or while he does it — so outcomes are unambiguous
Short, procedural utterances rather than long explanations — this is a quick baseline check, not a discussion
One brief comment about the physical wearing experience (comfort, audio placement) is natural and expected
Sigma's responses are clear, promptly delivered, and appropriately brief and close for a wearable assistant
No corner cases or failures occur in this scenario — it exists to establish that the basics work
The closing line sets up future testing without actually performing it
assistant_behavior: Sigma responds correctly to the wake word every time it is used in this scenario
Sigma answers each command and question accurately and concisely, in a tone appropriate to a wearable assistant
Sigma does not exhibit any errors, false triggers, or misunderstandings in this scenario
